grh_fd34ab36ed6d73a5043d.title: Melissa
paragraphs: Fourteen-year-old Melissa Baker and her mother move to a quiet California seaside town after the death of Melissa's father, only to become the center of a community panic. Melissa does not attend school because she possesses extraordinary knowledge and says that figures such as Albert Einstein and Leonardo da Vinci communicate with and teach her. A school inquiry cannot agree whether her experiences are psychic, psychological or supernatural, while one hostile official brands her evil and public fear grows into threats against the family. Melissa and her mother refuse to flee, and more than a hundred local young people gather at their home to protect her. Their insistence that no one can name any harm Melissa has actually caused forces some of the adults to confront how fear of difference, rather than Melissa herself, created the crisis.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Lucy Taylor, Mary Jane Croft, Tru Boardman, Norman Alden, and Marvin Miller. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Barney Gerard as writer, and [[person|vincent-price|Vincent Price]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_fdcf48bc85e8d7930ed0.title: Baldie
paragraphs: Bern becomes obsessed with his thinning hair just as he and his wife leave on a Nevada vacation with friends. After meeting a performer with an impressive head of hair, Bern eagerly waits for a promised carton of a product he thinks will restore his own. When it arrives, he rubs an entire tube into his scalp, only to wake up completely bald. At the manufacturer he learns that the carton was sent by mistake and the product was actually a depilatory meant to remove hair. To everyone's surprise, Bern decides he likes his new look, especially after learning the Lions Club now prefers him as master of ceremonies, and he jokes about completing the resemblance to Telly Savalas.

grh_fd95b203092ba22a7a06.title: Annie Laurie
paragraphs: This fictionalized story of Robert Burns begins with the struggling Scottish farmer and poet in love with Jean Armour, whose father refuses to accept him as a husband. Convinced he has no future in Scotland, Burns plans to sail for America. Jean secretly carries his poems to a publisher, and their success makes Burns famous before he can leave. He eventually learns that the idealized 'Annie Laurie' of his romantic imagination is not a rival at all but a poetic dream, while Jean is the real woman who believed in him and saved his work. Burns chooses Jean as his own Annie Laurie.

grh_fd3d2d9976de3f31ed96.title: Words at War 43-07-31 (06) from the Land of Silent People
paragraphs: A dramatized eyewitness report from Robert St. John's From the Land of Silent People recounts scenes from Yugoslavia and Greece as Axis occupation and war overwhelm civilian life. St. John's narrator describes bombings, refugees, military retreat, shortages and encounters with ordinary people trying to survive, including the recurring figure of Sonia. The program is structured as reportage rather than a single plot and closes with St. John reflecting on the occupied peoples who have been forced into silence but continue resistance while waiting for Allied liberation.
